newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to import 1.55 mln T of grain in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to import 1.55 mln T of grain in 1996/97.

text.p: Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday it would have to import some 1.55 million tonnes of grain for human and animal consumption to meet the country's 1996/97 needs of five million tonnes.

"Local farmers provided 3.29 million tonnes of grain for consumption and fodder so far and 125,000 tonnes of wheat came from former Yugoslavia in exchange for diesel oil produced in Neftohim," Deputy Agriculture minister Dimo Uzunov told a news conference. Neftohim is Bulgaria's biggest refinery.
He added that the cabinet hoped to negotiate an import deal for 250,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina which would be delivered between the beginning of January and the end of May.
The country was negotiating wheat imports with Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
Bulgaria faces an acute grain shortage following excessive exports last year and a poor harvest this summer due to adverse weather and a lack of funds.

At the beginning of October Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee to import 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat after Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line on the grounds that the conditions were unfavourable.

Lookin ahead, Uzunov said 500,000 hectares of wheat and barley had been sown by October 14, up from 350,000 ha sown on the same date last year. The ministry has set a planting target of some 1.6 ha of wheat and barley this autumn.
Last week Bulgaria's parliament approved a bill aimed at unblocking payments due to farmers from troubled banks in a bid to secure autumn sowings and stave off further grain shortages.
